messages:
Maya S.: Anyone else seeing GH Actions matrix runs hang on terraform in our infra repo? Several matrix jobs get to 'terraform init' then nothing, and other matrix entries complain about state lock timeouts.
Leo T.: Yep, saw 3 runs in a row this morning. Logs show init stuck at 'Acquiring state lock...' for > 10m.
Maya S.: Paste of snippet:
```
Run terraform init -input=false -no-color
Downloading modules...
Initializing the backend...
Acquiring state lock. This may take a few moments...
# nothing after this for 12+ minutes
```
Priya K.: Do we use actions/cache for .terraform directory in that workflow? Could be cache restore colliding between parallel matrix runners.
Maya S.: Yes, we cache .terraform/modules and .terraform/providers with a key: tf-${{ github.ref }}-modules. It's identical across matrix entries.
Winston G.: That key is too coarse. If two runners restore/extract the archive at the same time onto the same runner path (artifact race), you can get half-extracted dirs which break terraform init and then the backend lock logic times out waiting for operations to complete.
infra-bot: Reminder: workflow 'ci/infra' v6 started by maya-s at 2026-02-12T08:13:45Z
Leo T.: Quick repro: run the matrix with 4 parallel entries, then cancel one mid-restore. We saw corrupted .terraform with truncated provider files.
Zoe R.: Our fix in platform-services was to change cache key to include a checksum of .terraform.lock.hcl and runner-id in restore step, e.g., `key: tf-${{ github.ref }}-${{ hashFiles('.terraform.lock.hcl') }}-${{ runner.os }}-{{ matrix.os }}`. That reduces collisions and forces fresh provider installs when lockfile changed.
Priya K.: Can we also make the workflow use `concurrency` so only one terraform apply per branch runs at once? We used `concurrency: group: infra-${{ github.ref }}-tf` and `cancel-in-progress: false` so in-progress runs aren't cancelled (cancelling can leave locks weird) — but we still want plan steps to run in parallel for speed.
Maya S.: We prefer parallel plans (matrix) because different regions/azs take different providers, but applies must be serialized. Problem is init+plan still fails when cache is corrupted.
Winston G.: Another mitigation: run a lightweight preflight step that checks if `terraform init` completes within 60s; if not, delete the cached .terraform and re-run init. Example:
```
- name: tf init try
  run: |
    timeout 60 terraform init -input=false || (rm -rf .terraform && terraform init -input=false)
```
Zoe R.: That worked for us. Also set actions/cache `restore-keys` so we don't always restore an exact archive; plus enable compression level lower so extraction is faster and less likely to be preempted by runner lifecycle.
Leo T.: What about state locking? We're on S3+DynamoDB locks. Are cancelled runs leaving DynamoDB lock entries? You can always `terraform force-unlock` but can't do that in CI automatically.
Priya K.: DynamoDB has TTL for lock items? I thought the lock is owned until explicitly released. We saw a couple of runs that had the lock in TTl-like state due to runner preemption.
Winston G.: Correct, Terraform's state lock is held by a session id in DynamoDB record; if the runner dies it doesn't automatically release. TTL isn't a substitute. Best path is to avoid getting into the corrupted-init state in the first place, and serialize applies.
Maya S.: Proposed action items:
- Change cache key to include hash of .terraform.lock.hcl and runner/os metadata (Zoe)
- Add preflight init with fallback to clear cache if timed out (Winston)
- Add concurrency group for apply steps only, allow matrix plan parallelism but ensure apply serial (Priya)
- Add monitoring alert when terraform init/plan spends >5m in 'Acquiring state lock' (Maya)

Zoe R.: I'll open a PR with the cache key + preflight snippet.
Leo T.: I'll add a small GH Action that rejects workflow dispatch if there is an active apply for the same branch (webhook check) — low priority.
Maya S.: Thanks — let's keep this thread for follow-ups. If anyone hits the hang again, paste the `actions/toolkit` restore logs and the exact init output. :thumbsup:
